**Finding: deviation (NONCOMPETE, high severity) — Section 6.1 "Exclusivity" (¶p0037).**

**What I found.** The planner hint was right: the restriction on us is hidden inside the Exclusivity article, not under a non-compete heading. Section 6.1 bars *the Company* — our client — from participating in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products "or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including... the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to..." ).

**Why it fails the fallback.**
- **Scope is not a named competing product.** "Products substantially similar" and "companies similar to" is an elastic standard that sweeps in our core leather-apparel line generally.
- **No carve-out for internal development or acquisitions.** Section 6.2 carves out only a closeout-merchandise site, and the Deerskin Products definition (¶p0005) excludes the Joan Cook Catalog — neither covers building our own capability or a business we acquire.

**Why it is not walk-away.** The restriction is expressly "during the term of this Agreement" with no post-term tail (contrast Section 6.3, which binds HDI for the term plus two years — a restriction on the vendor, which we leave alone). The term is one year, auto-renewing annually and terminable on 90 days' notice; that can run past 12 months, but it is coextensive with the deal, so I noted it rather than redlined it.

**Redline (validated ok:true).** Because HDI's exclusive hosting bargain plausibly needs protection, I proposed the fallback narrowing rather than deletion: limit the restriction to Deerskin Products, and add carve-outs for (i) other products, (ii) internal development of web sites/e-commerce, and (iii) acquired or merged businesses.
